hypothesis: Layer 3 of the Author Proposition: systems disappear when their free-energy store F is exhausted at power P, so the steady number in a phase is N = b F/P (Little's law). For globular-cluster stars, which pass through the upper red giant branch and the horizontal branch once each (common b), R = N_HB/N_RGB equals the ratio of phase lifetimes from stellar models.

observable.quantity: R = N_HB / N_RGB(upper), weighted mean over 39 clusters
observable.domain: Galactic globular clusters with [M/H] < -1.1; 0.82-0.84 Msun stellar models

prediction_method.description: R_pred = 6.26 Y - 0.12 (stellar-model lifetime ratio) with Y = Y_HII_Aver; sigma_pred = 6.26 sigma_Y; z = |R_pred - R_obs| / sqrt(sigma_pred^2 + sigma_obs^2). Y_SBBN_as_used is reported as sensitivity only.

fixed_parameters: common formation rate b for RGB and HB
pass_criterion: z <= 2 with the primary helium input
fail_criterion: z > 3 with the primary helium input -> FAILED; 2 < z <= 3 -> INCONCLUSIVE (reported as tension, not pass)
note: Disclosure: drafted after reading the source, which itself reports that standard models (no axions) need Y = 0.241 +/- 0.005, compatible with the measured Y at about 2 sigma; the outcome is therefore close to the PASS/INCONCLUSIVE boundary and was effectively known before drafting. With the SBBN helium value the deviation would be smaller. T002 tests that layer 3 reproduces the established fuel-consumption reasoning (number in a phase proportional to its lifetime); it cannot distinguish UET from standard stellar astrophysics. Any residual tension corresponds, in layer-3 language, to an unmodelled extra burn channel shortening tau_HB (the source interprets it as possible axion cooling). Re-check transcribed numbers against the journal version before approval.
